_doc: Move-purity manifest. Each target declares the original file and its replacement PARTS, where every part records the ORIGINAL LINE RANGE it covers. catdiff.js asserts: (A) each part's bytes equal the pristine original's bytes for that range, (B) the ranges tile 1..N with no gap or overlap, (C) concatenating them reproduces the whole original byte-for-byte, (D) for client targets, the <script src> order parsed out of the real 'orderFrom' file equals the parts' ascending line order, and (E) every part's current on-disk sha256 matches a pin in clientPins -- the recoverable guarantee for a part declared modified:true, mirroring serverdiff's [SE]. A part with modified:true is EXPECTED to fail (A)/(C) against pristine and is skipped there by design; (E) is what keeps it honest instead, re-pinned deliberately in the same commit as any intentional change. Order is derived from the real HTML, never trusted from this file -- a disagreement between the two is reported as the bug. Check [5] (scriptblock.js) additionally validates the script block itself.
_lineEndings: This repo has core.autocrlf=true: files are CRLF on disk, LF in git blobs (app.js is 891641 bytes on disk vs 874347 in the blob -- exactly one extra byte per line). RAW byte-identity is MANDATORY for client parts; CRLF->LF is used only as a failure diagnostic and can never produce a PASS.

parts.modifiedReason: Added cachedIssueKey() (issue key from the already-loaded S.data cache), issueLabelFor() (openDrawer takes either an id or a key, so a load failure must cope with both) and issueSprintMoveText() -- one phrasing for "issue changed sprint", shared by the drawer picker and the backlog drag so the same action does not describe itself two ways.

The wrapper toasted e.message raw, so every unhandled failure showed "Internal server error" or a bare HTTP statusText. Now routed through errorReason(), which maps machine text to a readable clause and passes user-written API messages through untouched. Fixes the raw text at ~150 call sites at once rather than per site; sites that render their own message pass {silent:true} so one failure never stacks two toasts.

SECURITY (stored XSS): all three renderers built their text by concatenating the caller's message into innerHTML, so any markup in it executed. Real call sites interpolate user-controlled values -- an uploaded file's name (space-context-menu.js:371/398), a custom field's name (space/settings.js:737/741), a space name or key (crud/space.js:135/158/164, space/settings.js:786), a user's display name (admin-settings.js:417) and an invitee's email (admin-settings.js:501/520) -- so a file named `.png` ran on upload. toast() and toastWithButtons() now build every node with textContent; popupAlert() renders msg as textContent too, gated by a new allowHtmlMsg flag used by exactly one caller (admin-settings.js:507) that needs
to wrap a long invite URL and escapes its own interpolations. textContent was chosen over esc()-at-the-call-site so the vector is closed at the sink and a future caller cannot forget. Rendered output is unchanged: no toast message in the codebase contains markup or an HTML entity (verified by extracting all 214 literals from all 169 call sites and rendering each through the old and new implementations, 1603 comparisons, 0 differences in what the user reads), and each function's original falsy-handling is preserved exactly (toast renders "undefined", toastWithButtons renders "", matching concat vs esc() before). compare [1][2][2b][3][4] all empty.

The Summary tab's "Total Issues" stat card now navigates to All Work instead of Backlog -- the other four cards (To Do/In Progress/Done/Overdue) are unchanged, still go to Backlog with their status filter. Sets a one-shot window._awShowAllOverride flag before navigating; see all-work.js's _awLoadFilterState for why that flag exists instead of a setTimeout here.

Star toggle names the issue ("ENG-12 starred" / "ENG-12 unstarred", was "Issue starred" / "Star removed") and its failure gives a reason instead of "Could not update star". The catch was swallowing the error object entirely (catch (_)), so no reason was available to report; it now binds it.

The Summary tab never called refreshData() before rendering -- unlike All Work, which already guarded this -- so landing on Summary right after clicking a space could render getSpaceIssues() off stale/empty S.data and show every stat card as 0 despite the space having real issues. Extracted the shared 30s-staleness gate (previously inlined only in the 'allwork' case) into ensureSpaceDataFresh() and applied it to 'summary' too. Also: navigateTo()/navigateToSpace() now call window._gsReset() (global-search.js) so the top-bar search box's typed text doesn't survive a sidebar/breadcrumb navigation the way it used to.

formatDashboardActivity() now resolves a custom-field history row to its real field name (row.custom_field_name, from my-issues.js's new join) instead of the raw 'custom_field_<uuid>' -- and for the Product Type + Combination compound field specifically, diffs old_value/new_value (diffCombinationFieldChange) to say 'updated product type' vs 'updated combination' instead of always 'updated Combination', since one edit to either half writes a history row against that same field.

_renderYourWorkTable's last column is now a caller-chosen {label,key} instead of a fixed 'Updated' string: Assigned to Me shows Reporter (avatar+name) and Reported by Me shows Assignee (avatar+name) instead of an Updated timestamp on either -- Recently Viewed is unchanged (still Viewed, relative time). Server now joins reporter_name/reporter_color into the assigned-issues query (my-issues.js already had assignee_name on both).

Backlog drag names the issue and where it went, via the shared issueSprintMoveText(): "ENG-12 moved to Sprint 4" / "ENG-12 moved to the backlog" (was a bare "Issue moved"). The failure said "Failed to move issue - is the server running?", which guessed at a cause; it now reports the actual reason. Vocabulary ticket->issue.
Board drag-and-drop names the issue: "ENG-12 moved to In Progress" (was "Issue moved to In Progress").

Vocabulary ticket->issue across the bulk-delete permission message, the result message and the confirm dialog. The partial-failure message now states the denominator ("5 of 7 issues moved to Deleted Items - 2 failed") instead of two bare counts.

Vocabulary ticket->issue (the sprint-date warning, the delete permission message, and the delete dialog's own hint and button, which still said "ticket" while its toast said "issues"). Delete failure names the issue and the reason. Subtask creation uses the created row's own key ("ENG-13 created as a subtask") and its failure no longer toasts a bare e.message, which rendered an empty or "undefined" toast when the error carried no message. Drawer load failure names the issue and says why. Sprint-move text delegated to the shared issueSprintMoveText().

historyHtml()'s fieldLabel now resolves a custom-field history row via h.custom_field_name/h.custom_field_key (from issues.js's new join), same fix as space-header.js's dashboard activity feed and same reason -- the drawer's own History tab had the identical raw-field_name and misleading-Combination-label bugs. Uses the shared diffCombinationFieldChange() helper from utils/index.js.

Create/update messages name the issue: "ENG-12 created" on all four create paths (the key is on the POST response already), "ENG-12 created - opening...", "ENG-12 created, attachments failed - <reason>". "Failed to create issue: <raw>" became "Issue creation failed - <reason>", and the POST is now {silent:true} so it is one toast rather than the raw one plus mine. The edit path stays a generic "<KEY> updated": it saves many fields at once without diffing them, and naming a field would need a server change or a client-side diff. NOTE: that edit branch is currently unreachable -- nothing ever sets #issueId (only clears it), so the modal cannot open on an existing issue.

openNotifTarget() navigated sprint_started/sprint_completed notifications to a tab literally named 'board' -- but the app's tab for that view is 'sprint' (Active Sprint), and there is no 'board' case in renderTab()'s switch, so the click silently rendered nothing. Now routes sprint_started -> 'sprint' and sprint_completed -> 'reports' (its real link target per notification-triggers.md), both by type and by matching the link's URL segment directly. sprint_completed additionally checks canManageSpace() first: Reports is site_admin-only, so a plain member goes to 'backlog' instead (the completed sprint's issues spilled back there) rather than hitting a permission-denied toast.

SECURITY (stored XSS), paired with toast.js: the 'Invitation Resent / email not sent' popupAlert is the ONLY caller in the app that deliberately renders markup (a
so a long invite URL wraps instead of overflowing). popupAlert now defaults msg to textContent, so this call opts back in with the new allowHtmlMsg flag and escapes its own three interpolations (email, email_reason, invite_url) with esc(). Verified: the
and still render as real elements with the wrap style intact, while a hostile email/URL renders as literal text and fires nothing.

Added window._gsReset(), called from navigateTo()/navigateToSpace() in navigation.js -- the search box lives in the top bar outside every swapped view, so typed text used to survive any sidebar/breadcrumb navigation (only picking a search RESULT cleared it before).

conventions.lineCounting: part.from/part.to are SPLIT-ELEMENT indices into pristine content split on newline, NOT newline counts. A file with N newlines yields N+1 split elements, the last being the empty string after the final newline. global-search.js: 476 newlines (wc -l), elements 16819-17295 = 477. Pristine app.js: 17294 newlines / 17295 elements. Sum of wc -l over all 42 client files = 17294. Neither number is wrong -- see AUDIT-FINDINGS.md.
conventions.moves: targets[].moves declares intentional relocations of a block between split files. Contiguity is deliberately broken for the files involved: catdiff [A] becomes move-aware (pristine MINUS blocks moved out, PLUS blocks moved in at the declared position) and [C] becomes REVERSIBILITY -- un-apply every declared move against the files actual bytes and require pristine back line-for-line.
conventions.libPins: lib/ has no pristine original to tile against -- it is hand-written code predating the refactor -- so libdiff.js pins a sha256 per file instead. Any byte change fails [L1] until the pin is updated in the SAME commit with a reason. Unlike serverdiff modified:true, a pin is RESTORED on re-pinning, so lib/ coverage does not decay.
